name: Grade 7 IIIT: Credible Sources and Blog Media
description: Source credibility, plagiarism, citation, Creative Commons, blog features, captions, headings, layout, calls to action, and cause-based media posts.

words.definition: The place where information or media comes from.
words.example: The source included a link and author.

words.definition: Trustworthy and supported by useful evidence.
words.example: A credible source listed an author and date.

words.definition: The person or group that created information or media.
words.example: The student checked the author of the article.

words.definition: Information that supports an idea or claim.
words.example: The article used evidence from research.

words.definition: The reason a source or message was created.
words.example: The source purpose was to persuade readers.

words.definition: Using someone else's work or ideas without proper credit.

words.example: The citation included title, author, and link.

words.definition: A note that names the creator or source of media.
words.example: The photo had a credit below it.

words.definition: Rules explaining how someone may use creative work.
words.example: The image license allowed reuse with credit.

words.definition: An online post or page used to share ideas or updates.
words.example: The blog post supported a cause.

words.definition: Text that names a section or topic.
words.example: The heading introduced the main idea.

words.definition: Text that explains an image or media item.
A group of sentences about one idea.
The arrangement of text, images, and other elements.
words.example: The layout made the blog easier to read.

words.definition: A message that asks the audience to do something.
words.example: The call to action asked readers to recycle batteries.

words.definition: An issue or goal that people support.
words.example: The blog promoted an environmental cause.

words.definition: An early version of writing or design.
words.example: The draft was revised after feedback.

words.definition: The practice of recording and showing sources.
words.example: Referencing helped the reader verify information.
